title: Console theming: token mapping, component overrides, and brand theme variants for dark mode
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Define a pragmatic token mapping and component override approach to fully support dark mode and multiple brand themes in the Redwood Console without a breaking migration for existing applications. Scope covers core tokens (colors, elevation, spacing, typography), component-level overrides for Buttons/Tables/Charts, token alias strategy, and a migration plan for CSS variables and component props.

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic token mapping that allows theme composition (base -> brand -> mode).
- Allow component teams to opt-in to overrides (e.g., button brand fills) via a documented API.
- Ship a dark-mode-ready chart palette and table row/selection states that maintain accessibility (AA contrast).
- Minimize runtime work and avoid large style recalculations on theme switch.

Constraints & considerations:
- Must support both hosted Console theming and private deployments with customer brand overrides.
- Engineering prefers CSS custom properties at the root for fast theme switching; we need a clear mapping from design tokens to CSS variables.
- Some legacy components use hard-coded values; migration guidance and fallbacks required.
- Chart library (internal wrapper around Recharts) needs an explicit palette and token access.

Key artifacts:
- Figma theme file (draft): https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/redwood-console-themes
- Token spec (working): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Token+Mapping+Spec
- Prototype (storybook): https://staging.storybook.redwood.ai/?path=/story/theme-switcher--dark-mode

Acceptance criteria:
- Token mapping doc completed and reviewed by Eng and PM (links in comments).
- Figma components updated with token aliases and dark variants for Buttons, Tables, and Charts.
- Storybook demo that shows theme composition (default, brand-violet, brand-amber) and dark toggle with <100ms switch.
- Migration checklist for legacy components and a plan for a 2-week compatibility window.

Deliverables:
- Token mapping spec with name space (e.g., --rwd-bg-base, --rwd-text-primary) and alias rules.
- Component override patterns: prop-level overrides, CSS variable fallbacks, and theme tokens table.
- Chart palette with accessible color pairs for lines/areas/points and a guidance doc for chart authors.
- Figma updates + Storybook examples.

2026-02-24 Ethan Park (Engineering): Reviewed token approach. Prefer root CSS vars for quick toggles. Raised concern about kv-cache UI that renders server side and needs to hydrate theme on first paint. Suggested a small hydration script and fallback tokens. Linking internal RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/124

2026-03-01 Maya Chen: Updated Figma with token aliases and added dark variants for button and table components. Requested design review on contrast ratios. See Figma frames: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/redwood-console-themes?node-id=512%3A10

2026-03-05 Arun Nair (Accessibility): Ran contrast checks. Found selection state in table (selected row + focus ring) fails AA in dark mode for low-density palettes. Recommendation: increase selection fill opacity and adjust focus ring to neutral-strong token. Added specific color suggestions to Confluence doc.

2026-03-07 PR opened (ENG): PR #9876 implements root CSS var mapping and theme switcher micro-API. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/9876. Engineering notes request a final token naming pass and a migration guide for components still using SCSS variables.

2026-03-10 Design review (internal): Consensus to use a three-layer composition: base tokens -> mode aliases -> brand overrides. Decision: component-level overrides should prefer token aliases over inline styles to keep runtime light. Action: produce a token table mapping old token names to new CSS vars for a 1:1 migration.

2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Added chart palette proposal to Confluence and Storybook. Proposed 8-color palette with 4 high-contrast pairs for dark and light. Link to story: https://staging.storybook.redwood.ai/?path=/story/charts--color-palette

2026-03-14 Ethan Park (Engineering): Implemented prototype story and performance test. Theme switch measured at ~60ms in dev build and ~28ms in production build. Noted one regression: legacy table component still calculates inline styles on render due to old SCSS mixin. Created ENG-4189 to track removal of hard-coded values.

2026-03-14 Maya Chen: Next steps: finalize token naming (PR draft in Confluence), write migration checklist for component owners, pair with ENG on SCSS->CSS var migration, and schedule cross-team sync next Tue.
